newsitem.title: USA: CFTC says Besner permanently barred from futures.
newsitem.headline: CFTC says Besner permanently barred from futures.

text.p: The Commodity Futures Trading Commission (CFTC) said Robert Besner, president of commodity trading adviser New Forest Capital Management Inc, was permanently barred from the U.S. futures markets by a U.S. District Court.

U.S. District Judge John Nordberg entered a consent order of permanent injunction against Besner and New Forest last week after the CFTC alleged in January 1996 that Besner defrauded investors by misappropriating customer funds.
About $2.2 million is unaccounted for out of $2.7 million Besner accepted from clients, the CFTC said.

"We are trying to amicably settle this matter with the CFTC, provide the accounting and agree that this injunctive order -- with the finding in it -- could be entered," Ted Helwig, Besner's attorney, said.
The injunction said Besner must turn over all accounting records within 30 days.
Besner, who was feared to have fled around the time of the CFTC's five-count injunction on January 4, 1996, is no longer a resident of Chicago, Helwig said.
"He is no longer a resident in Chicago, but he has always been available and accessible through his counsel," he said, declining to specify Besner's whereabouts.
Helwig said Besner has been cooperating with the FBI.

He also said Besner's records have been turned over to the trustee of the bankruptcy case that Besner's clients filed against New Forest, Besner and his wife in U.S. bankruptcy court. -Derivatives desk 312-408-8750;E-mail derivatives@reuter.com
